chose: The Game Week essay's template is the third data essay, beside the Rust Rounds and interview essays: its own DNA (`some-ui.game-essay/1`: the week, the team it is read for, games, their halves with bites, halftime, the open and the close) on the shared helpers (`Format`, `nightInMotion`, `Parsed`, `problemsOf`, `once`, `weekId`), with scenes open, game, bite, halftime and close. Section 0's four rules (D20) are held by the schema where a type can hold them and checked where it can't: a scene is made only from a bite and a half or game with none is refused; a bite carries one still at most, of the play home matched it to, and none when unmatched (D12); a bite's stance is one of the five of D21, each answered by the host its own way in a total record; and a host line repeating a run of a matched play's text is refused at parse, before anything renders. The owner's own words are not held to that rule. Scenes, the cut list and the stage wait for home's week file.
options: A third data essay, with the rules held by type and one check (chosen): two members already share this shape, and a rule the type holds can't be written around.
A cards essay (a cut list written directly): its scenes are free shots, so section 0's first two rules would be checks over any shot instead of shapes the data can't take.

Lift a generic data-essay kind first, then add this as its member: the two members share helpers already, and their DNA, which is what differs, is per kind by nature; the lift is due when a third shared step appears (the recorder's `EssayKind`), not before.
All four rules as runtime checks, as D20 words them: a check is one more thing that can be skipped, where a type can't be.
gray: D20 says the four rules are checked by code before anything renders, without saying by which mechanism, and the essay could join either essay family; the owner would see the difference in what a writer can and cannot hand home.
